review_comments.body:
Precision and Recall use a different "present" class set than IoU/F1, because the mask is `denominator > 0` and each metric has its own denominator. A class that exists in the ground truth but is never predicted has `tp + fp == 0`. It is therefore dropped from the Precision mean instead of scoring 0. That is the failure this PR is fixing for IoU: a model that never finds the object looks better than it should. Example: targets have buildings, preds are all background. Recall averages over both classes, giving 0.5. Precision averages over background only, giving about 0.83, even though the model missed every building.

Consider building `present` from the ground truth plus predictions (`tp + fp + fn > 0`) for all four metrics. Define a class's precision as 0 when `tp + fp == 0`. For example: `present = (tp + fp + fn) > 0`, then `numerator[present] / denominator[present].clamp(min=1)`.

Confidence: medium. This may be intended, but it is inconsistent with the stated goal and the tests don't cover Precision in this case.

** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Move the pooled matrix to CPU before converting to float64.** When `device` is MPS, `.double()` raises because MPS does not support float64 tensors. GeoAI's `get_device()` selects MPS on supported Apple Silicon systems, so this change prevents validation from returning metrics there. ([docs.pytorch.org](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/notes/mps.html)) Use `confusion.cpu().double()` here. This preserves pooled integer counts and keeps the final calculations compatible with CPU, CUDA and MPS.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Version the selection metric in checkpoints before comparing resumed IoU.** `resume_training` restores `best_score` from the checkpoint without change. The epoch loop then compares the new pooled `val_iou` with that value. A checkpoint written before this change stores a per-image-average IoU. Pooled IoU can be lower than that baseline even when the model improves. In that case, the run does not save `best_model.pth`, and early stopping advances. Training can stop before a better model is saved. Store a metric version in each checkpoint. When a resumed checkpoint lacks the current version, reset the selection baseline or recompute it with the pooled metric before the first comparison. Keep the current comparison for same-version checkpoints and for `monitor="val_loss"`.

✅ Addressed in commit 428a39d

Precision is averaged only over classes that were predicted (`tp+fp > 0`), so a class that exists in the targets but is never predicted is dropped from the mean instead of scoring 0. In the first test, the "building" class has TP=0 and FN=32, and it contributes 0 to IoU and Recall but nothing to Precision. As a result, Precision can look better than it should, and it is averaged over a different set of classes than IoU, F1 and Recall. If you want consistent class sets, define the scored classes as those with any target support (`confusion.sum(dim=1) > 0`) and treat 0/0 precision as 0. At the least, document the current behavior (confidence: medium).

Nit: `pred_classes` comes from `argmax(outputs, dim=1)`, so it is always in `[0, outputs.shape[1])`. This check does nothing unless the model emits more channels than `num_classes`. In that case it silently drops those pixels instead of flagging the mismatch. Consider removing it, or raising or warning when `outputs.shape[1] != num_classes`. Confidence: low.

** Minor** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win** **Reset incompatible `best_iou` for loss-monitored resumes too.** If an unversioned `val_loss` checkpoint contains `best_iou=0.9`, this guard preserves that per-image value. Subsequent pooled IoUs of 0.5 cannot replace it. The next checkpoint stores 0.9 with `val_iou_version=2`, and the training summary reports an incompatible maximum. On a version mismatch, reset `best_iou` for either monitor. Reset `best_score` and `best_epoch` only for `val_iou`. This preserves loss-based selection and same-version resume behavior.

**Explanation** The title "fix(train): pool TP/FP/FN over the loader in evaluate_semantic" matches the main change. The PR changes evaluate_semantic to pool a confusion matrix across the validation loader instead of averaging per-image metrics. The title names the function, the pooling change, and the affected module. The PR also includes related changes, such as the validation-IoU versioning for checkpoint resume, which the title does not mention. That omission is expected for a short title.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Directly linked issue `#984` requires dataset-level pooled IoU, F1, precision and recall in evaluate_semantic. Requirements: (1) one num_classes x num_classes confusion matrix over the loader; (2) drop pixels with target equal to ignore_index or outside the class range; (3) average each metric over classes with a non-zero denominator; (4) keep return keys unchanged; (5) leave standalone metric functions untouched. The previous assessment verified these in geoai/train.py (torch.bincount accumulation, pooled tp/fp/fn, _mean_over_present excluding an in-range ignore_index) and recomputed the hand-computed test case. The changes since the previous review, per the raw summary, add a checkpoint version (_VAL_IOU_VERSION = 2) and a CPU move before float64 conversion. These do not change the pooled metric definition. Tests in tests/test_evaluate_semantic_pooled.py cover the pooled value, model ordering, batch-size independence, ignored targets (255, -100), and the in-range ignore_index class. The claim that 4 of 5 new tests fail before the change was not executed and is not verified. The incremental diff could not be read (changed blobs unavailable), so the post-review code evidence rests on the supplied summaries.

**Explanation** The whole-PR scope is geoai/train.py (evaluate_semantic metric body, and train_segmentation_model resume handling), tests/test_evaluate_semantic_pooled.py, and tests/test_train_kfold.py. The new resume logic (_VAL_IOU_VERSION; resetting best_score and best_iou when a monitor="val_iou" checkpoint lacks or mismatches the version) addresses a consequence of the changed IoU definition: an old best_score is not comparable to the new pooled IoU. ## Code review

I reviewed the changes to `evaluate_semantic` in `geoai/train.py` and the new `tests/test_evaluate_semantic_pooled.py`. I only read the code. I did not run the tests.

### Bugs
- **Precision and Recall average over different class sets than IoU and F1** (medium confidence, inline comment posted). The code averages only over classes whose denominator is above 0. A class that is in the ground truth but never predicted has `tp + fp == 0`, so it is dropped from the Precision mean instead of scoring 0. For example, if the targets contain buildings and the model predicts only background, Recall is 0.5 and Precision is about 0.83. That inflates Precision in the same case this PR is meant to fix for IoU. Using `(tp + fp + fn) > 0` as the class mask for all four metrics, and scoring 0 where the denominator is 0, would be more consistent.

### Security
- None found.

### Performance
- The pooled confusion matrix is faster than the old per-image loop. `torch.bincount` runs on the device and avoids the per-sample metric calls. No concerns.

### Quality
- The pooling logic is correct. The mask covers valid targets, in-range predictions and `ignore_index`. The result does not depend on batch size, and the new tests check that. Low-confidence nit: `avg_loss = total_loss / num_batches` raises `ZeroDivisionError` on an empty loader. This was already the case before the PR.
- The new tests cover the hand-computed value, batch-size independence, all-ignore tiles and an in-range `ignore_index`. They have no Precision assertion for a class that is never predicted, which is the case in the Bugs item above.

### CLAUDE.md
- No applicable CLAUDE.md guideline violations found.

## Code review

The pooled-confusion-matrix approach is sound. It is independent of batch size, correctly masks `ignore_index` and out-of-range labels, and the new tests cover the main edge cases. I found one behavioral concern and a few minor points. I only read the diff and the surrounding code, and did not run the tests.

### Bugs
- **Precision averaging is inconsistent with the other metrics (medium confidence).** `_mean_over_present` averages precision only over classes with `tp+fp > 0`. A class that is present in the targets but never predicted is therefore dropped from the Precision mean rather than scoring 0. The same class counts as 0 in IoU, F1 and Recall. Precision can end up inflated, and the metrics are averaged over different class sets. I left an inline comment on `geoai/train.py:4040`. Scoring over classes with target support would make the four metrics consistent.

### Security
- None found.

### Performance
- None found. The pooled `bincount` is cheaper than the previous per-sample metric loops.

### Quality
- **Behavior change (low confidence).** `evaluate_semantic` now returns dataset-level metrics instead of per-image means, so numbers will differ from earlier runs and anything keyed on them (for example best-model selection or logged baselines). That seems intended, but a changelog or docstring note would help. The docstring doesn't mention pooling.
- **Edge case (low confidence).** If `ignore_index` is in range and every valid pixel belongs to that class, all metrics return 0.0 silently.
- **Missing `Optional[int]` handling (nit).** `0 <= ignore_index < num_classes` is fine, but `valid &= targets != ignore_index` is redundant with the range mask whenever `ignore_index` is out of range.
- **Dead code (nit).** `f1_score`, `iou_coefficient`, `precision_score` and `recall_score` are still defined but no longer used in `train.py`. They are likely public API, so keep them.

### CLAUDE.md
- No applicable guideline violations found.

Thanks for picking this up. This is the same change as the fix I had locally for #984: one pooled `bincount` confusion matrix, targets outside `[0, num_classes)` or equal to `ignore_index` dropped, an in-range `ignore_index` left out of the class mean, and each metric averaged over the classes with a non-zero denominator. So I won't open a second PR. Going by the diff, it gives the "Dataset-level mIoU" column of the table in #984.

On the open precision comment: skipping a class with no predicted pixels comes from the old per-image `precision_score`, which does the same (`if predicted_positives > 0`), and my version kept that rule too. scikit-learn 1.9.1 and torchmetrics 1.9.0 instead score such a class as 0 in macro precision. For the #984 model that never predicts buildings, they give 0.4375, where this PR gives 0.875. Matching the libraries would put all four metrics on the same classes; keeping the old rule would match what geoai reported before.

_Written with help from an AI assistant (Claude). I read the diff but did not run this PR's code; the library numbers come from a separate script._

Thanks for the reviews. Pushed a commit addressing the two CodeRabbit threads:

- The pooled confusion matrix is moved to CPU before `.double()`, so validation also works on MPS (no float64 there).
- Checkpoints now store a `val_iou_version`. Resuming a `val_iou` run from a checkpoint without it resets the best-IoU baseline, since the old value was a per-image mean and is not comparable with the pooled IoU; same-version checkpoints and `val_loss` runs are unchanged. A test covers both cases.

On Precision averaging (raised in the github-actions review and by @FasterThanAi): I left it as is on purpose. It keeps the previous `precision_score` rule (skip classes with no predicted pixels), so reported Precision stays comparable with earlier geoai numbers. Scoring such a class as 0 (as scikit-learn and torchmetrics do) is a one-line change in `_mean_over_present`; @giswqs, do you prefer matching those libraries?

_Written with help from an AI assistant (Claude); the change was tested with `pytest tests/test_train_kfold.py tests/test_evaluate_semantic_pooled.py` (76 passed)._

## Code review

I read the diff and the surrounding `evaluate_semantic` code. I did not run the tests. `evaluate_semantic` now pools a confusion matrix over the whole loader instead of averaging per-image scores. The pooled math (IoU, F1, precision and recall from TP/FP/FN) looks correct. The CPU float64 move for MPS, batch-size independence, `ignore_index` handling and the checkpoint-version reset on resume all look sound.

### Bugs
- None found.

### Security
- None found.

### Performance
- None found. Pooling with `bincount` on-device is cheaper than the old per-sample loop.

### Quality
- **Redundant prediction range check** (`geoai/train.py:4016`). The check on `pred_classes` is dead code, because `argmax` output is always in range. If a model emits more channels than `num_classes`, it silently drops pixels instead of flagging the mismatch. Consider removing it or warning on a channel mismatch. Confidence: low.
- **Behavior change:** the metrics returned by `evaluate_semantic` now mean something different, with absent classes excluded and ignored classes dropped. Existing users will see different values. The checkpoint version bump covers resume, and a changelog or docs note would help.
- **Minor test gap:** the tests cover pooled values, batch-size independence and in-range or out-of-range `ignore_index`. There is no test where `num_batches == 0` or where no class is present, which should return 0.0.

### CLAUDE.md
- No CLAUDE.md issues found in the changed files.
